description: Revising a business rule that earlier changes copied, in Go (standard library only). permitctl, a borough council's resident parking permit tool with tests, a README, and six commits of history, has three commands that each charge for a permit: quote (internal/quote, the website's application form, where the rule was first written), renewals (internal/renewals, the monthly renewal letters, a copy written as a switch), and forecast (internal/forecast, the budget's income forecast, a copy whose band comparison came out exclusive). The rule is a charge by CO2 band (a vehicle exactly on a band's upper figure is in that band), a diesel surcharge, and a surcharge for the second and later permits at an address. Two later charge changes each reached only some copies, so today the quote charges 50.00 for later permits, the letters charge band C at 90.00, and the forecast puts a vehicle exactly on a band figure in the next band, where docs/permit-charges.md says 60.00, 96.00, and that band; the history shows how. The request is next year's change, already written into docs/permit-charges.md (a new band G over 255 g/km at 292.00, band F stopping at 255, the diesel surcharge 45.00 instead of 30.00), for the quote, the renewal letters, and the forecast; it names neither the copies, nor that they disagree, nor how to fix them, and the charges page says permitctl uses it for everything it works out. Editing all three copies (and fixing each copy's drift) passes the visible tests and every hidden case today. Required: builds (`go build -o permitctl ./cmd/permitctl` offline in bubblewrap, the hidden exports never visible to a build); existing_tests_pass (the fixture's money, permits, and command-line tests, placed over the agent's tree with every other test file removed, run by name); existing_behavior_kept (hidden cases of an export with a byte-order mark and Windows line endings, reordered columns and any-case values, refusals, a month with no renewals, bad command lines); new_policy_charged (all three commands exact on hidden inputs where the fixture's copies, with the request applied, would agree); drift_resolved (all three exact, as docs/permit-charges.md gives, on hidden inputs where those copies disagree); all_follow_rule_edits: after the agent's change the rule is edited again twelve ways (band C up and down, band G up, the diesel surcharge up and down, the later-permit surcharge up and down, band D's figure down, band F's up, every band charge up by 4.00 at once, the band comparison made exclusive, and the later-permit surcharge starting at the third permit), each at one place found by behavior in the check's copy of the agent's tree, rebuilt, and the quote, the letters, and the forecast must all print what the edited rule gives, so a copy of any value, of the band comparison, or of the later-permit condition fails; one_rule_definition: at most one of the program's files (Go outside tests, testdata, docs, and vendor, and files it names or embeds) holds the band charges. Measures: edits followed by each command and where they landed, builds, table files, the rule's file and whether each consumer package reaches it, charges elsewhere, the fixture's tests, the agent's own suite, test files changed, whether docs/permit-charges.md changed, files changed, commits. Needs bubblewrap and the host's Go (TRIAL_GOROOT overrides it); agent arms need Go readable only when it lives under the home. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Cabinet approved next year's permit charges last week, and Priya put them in docs/permit-charges.md: there's a new band G for the biggest polluters, and the diesel surcharge goes up. Could you get permitctl onto them? The website quote, the renewal letters, and finance's forecast all need the new charges; the first letters go out for April renewals.
